metadata.title: Boundary behavior for a singular quasi-linear elliptic equation

extraction_notes.note: The proof of Theorem 1.1 is the whole of Section 2 in running text (no proof environment); the node runs from 'In this section, we prove Theorem~\ref{main}.' to the \qed, before Remarks 2.1-2.3.
Equations (2.2), (2.5), (2.8) are intermediate limits announced with 'we now prove that' and proved in place; kept as equation nodes (not claims) since the text never names them as results.
problem or assumption: the opening sentence states the boundary value problem (1.1) together with the standing hypotheses (1.2) on a and f; kept as one problem node containing both equations.
The description of the explosive-solution problem studied in [GlasquII] (related work, with an unnumbered display) and the motivational sentences of the introduction get no node.

nodes.name: Smooth bounded domain $\Omega$
nodes.statement: Let $\Omega\subset{\mathbb R}^N$ be a smooth bounded domain.

nodes.name: Singular quasi-linear Dirichlet problem
nodes.statement: The aim of this note is to establish existence, uniqueness and boundary behavior of the solutions to the singular quasi-linear problem \begin{equation} \begin{cases} \,-{\rm div}(a(u)Du)+\frac{a'(u)}{2}|Du|^2=f(u) & \text{in $\Omega$,} \\ \,\, u>0 & \text{in $\Omega$,} \\ \,\, u=0 & \text{on $\partial\Omega$,} \end{cases} \end{equation} where $a:(0,+\infty)\to (0,+\infty)$ is a $C^1$ function bounded away from zero, $f:(0,+\infty)\to (0,+\infty)$ is a $C^1$ function and there exist $a_0>0$ and $f_0>0$ such that \begin{align} \lim_{s\to 0^+} a(s)s^{2\mu}=a_0, & \qquad\text{for some $0\leq \mu<1$}, \\ \lim_{s\to 0^+} f(s)s^\gamma=f_0, & \qquad\text{for some $\gamma>1$}, \\ 2f'(s)a(s)\leq f(s)a'(s), & \qquad\text{for every $s>0$}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Find positive solutions of $-\mathrm{div}(a(u)Du)+\frac{a'(u)}{2}|Du|^2=f(u)$ vanishing on $\partial\Omega$, with $a\sim a_0 s^{-2\mu}$, $f\sim f_0 s^{-\gamma}$ near $0$.

nodes.name: Singular quasi-linear problem (1.1)
nodes.statement: \begin{cases} \,-{\rm div}(a(u)Du)+\frac{a'(u)}{2}|Du|^2=f(u) & \text{in $\Omega$,} \\ \,\, u>0 & \text{in $\Omega$,} \\ \,\, u=0 & \text{on $\partial\Omega$,} \end{cases}
nodes.label: prob

nodes.name: Asymptotic and monotonicity conditions on a and f (1.2)
nodes.statement: \lim_{s\to 0^+} a(s)s^{2\mu}=a_0, & \qquad\text{for some $0\leq \mu<1$}, \\ \lim_{s\to 0^+} f(s)s^\gamma=f_0, & \qquad\text{for some $\gamma>1$}, \\ 2f'(s)a(s)\leq f(s)a'(s), & \qquad\text{for every $s>0$}.
nodes.statement_short: $a(s)s^{2\mu}\to a_0$, $f(s)s^\gamma\to f_0$ as $s\to0^+$, and $2f'a\le fa'$.
nodes.label: ass-a

nodes.name: Distance to the boundary ${\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)$
nodes.statement: Under assumptions \eqref{ass-a}-\eqref{ass-fg}, if ${\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)$ denotes the distance of a point $x$ in $\Omega$ from the boundary $\partial\Omega$, we shall prove the following
nodes.genus: the distance of a point $x$ in $\Omega$ from the boundary $\partial\Omega$

nodes.name: Existence, uniqueness and boundary behavior for the singular quasi-linear problem
nodes.statement: Problem~\eqref{prob} has a unique solution $u\in C^2(\Omega)\cap C(\bar\Omega)$ and there exist $\Gamma,\Gamma',\Gamma''>0$ with \begin{align*} \Gamma{\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{\frac{2}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}\leq u(x)\leq \Gamma' {\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{\frac{2}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}, \quad |Du(x)|\leq \Gamma''{\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{\frac{1-\gamma+2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}},&\quad\,\, \text{as ${\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)\to 0$.} \end{align*} Moreover $u\in {\rm Lip}(\bar\Omega)$ if $1<\gamma\leq 1+2\mu$, $u\in C^{0,\frac{2}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}(\bar\Omega)$ if $\gamma>1+2\mu$ and $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ if $\gamma<3-2\mu$.
nodes.statement_short: Problem (1.1) has a unique classical solution with $u\asymp d^{2/(1+\gamma-2\mu)}$ and a gradient bound near $\partial\Omega$; Lipschitz, H\"older or $H^1_0$ regularity depending on $\gamma,\mu$.
conclusions: Problem~\eqref{prob} has a unique solution $u\in C^2(\Omega)\cap C(\bar\Omega)$
nodes.label: main

nodes.name: Competition between a and f in the vanishing rate
nodes.statement: Whence, in some sense, the functions $a$ and $f$ compete for the vanishing rate of the solution and for its gradient upper bound, near the boundary $\partial\Omega$.

nodes.name: Enlarged range of Lipschitz continuity
nodes.statement: Furthermore, the range for Lipschitz continuity of $u$ up to the boundary is $\gamma\leq 1+2\mu$, $\gamma\neq 1$ thus enlarged with respect to the one for the semi-linear case, namely $0<\gamma<1$, see also Remark~\ref{globalrem}.

nodes.name: Growth of a and decay of f at infinity
nodes.statement: Without loss of generality we assume that $a$ grows as $s^k$ and $f$ decays as $s^{-p}$ as $s\to+\infty$ for some $k\geq 0$ and $p>1$, in which case one can also obtain estimates for $u$ and $|Du|$ valid on the whole $\bar\Omega$, as pointed out in Remark~\ref{globalrem}.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG $a$ grows like $s^k$ ($k\ge0$) and $f$ decays like $s^{-p}$ ($p>1$) at infinity.

nodes.name: Semi-linear case $a\equiv 1$
nodes.statement: In the particular case when $a\equiv 1$, problem \eqref{prob} reduces to $-\Delta u =f(u)$ and the above estimates reduce to $\Gamma{\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{2/(1+\gamma)}\leq u(x)\leq \Gamma' {\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{2/(1+\gamma)}$ and $|Du(x)|\leq \Gamma''{\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{(1-\gamma)/(1+\gamma)}$ as ${\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)\to 0$, consistently with the results of \cite{craRabTar,zhangcheng}.
nodes.statement_short: For $a\equiv1$ the estimates reduce to $u\asymp d^{2/(1+\gamma)}$, $|Du|\lesssim d^{(1-\gamma)/(1+\gamma)}$, as known for $-\Delta u=f(u)$.

nodes.name: Extensions to non-autonomous nonlinearities and unbounded domains
nodes.statement: Following the line of \cite{lairshak,zhangcheng}, some easy adaptations of Theorem~\ref{main} can be obtained to cover the case of non-autonomous nonlinearities such as $q(x)f(u)$ in place of $f(u)$ and of unbounded domains of ${\mathbb R}^N$. We leave these further developments to the interested reader.

nodes.name: Example of admissible a and f
nodes.statement: As an example of $f$ and $a$ satisfying \eqref{ass-a}-\eqref{ass-fg} one can take $f(s)=s^{-\gamma}$, $a(s)=s^{-2\mu}$ for $s\leq s_0$ and $a(s)=\theta(s)$ for $s\geq s_0$ for some $s_0>0$, with $\theta\in C^1\cap L^\infty$ bounded away from zero, $\theta(s_0)=s_0^{-2\mu}$, $\theta'(s_0)=-2\mu s_0^{-2\mu-1}$ and $s\theta'(s)+2\gamma \theta(s)\geq 0$ for $s\geq s_0$.
nodes.statement_short: $f(s)=s^{-\gamma}$ with $a=s^{-2\mu}$ near $0$, glued $C^1$ to a bounded $\theta$ satisfying $s\theta'+2\gamma\theta\ge0$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.1
nodes.statement:
In this section, we prove Theorem~ef{main}. We shall assume that conditions \eqref{ass-a}-\eqref{ass-fg} hold. In order to get information about existence, uniqueness and the boundary behavior of the solutions to \eqref{prob}, we convert the quasi-linear problem \eqref{prob} into a corresponding semi-linear problem through a change of variable procedure involving the Cauchy problem for $g\in C^2((0,+\infty))\cap C([0,+\infty))$,  egin{equation}  egin{cases} g'(s)= rac{1}{\sqrt{a(g(s))}},\quad 	ext{for $s>0$}, &\ g(0)=0, & \ 
oalign{\vskip3pt} g(s)>0, \quad	ext{for $s>0$}. & \end{cases} \end{equation} Due to the requirement $g>0$, the solutions of~\eqref{cauchy} are unique and solve $\int_0^{g(s)}\sqrt{a(\xi)}d\xi=s$, for $s>0$. The solution is global for $s>0$ since $a$ is bounded away from zero. This procedure was also followed in \cite{GlasquII} in the framework of explosive solutions, although there $g$ is $C^2$ around the origin and defined on ${\mathbb R}$. Now, since $g\in C^2((0,+\infty))\cap C([0,+\infty))$ and it is strictly increasing, it is readily seen by a direct computation that $u\in C^2(\Omega)\cap C( ar\Omega)$ is a positive solution to \eqref{prob} if and only if $v=g^{-1}(u)\in C^2(\Omega)\cap C( ar\Omega)$ is a positive solution to $-\Delta v=h(v)$ in $\Omega$, where we have set $h(s):=f(g(s))/\sqrt{a(g(s))}$ for $s>0$. Let us now obtain the asymptotic behavior of the solution $g$ to problem~\eqref{cauchy} as $s	o 0^+$ depending of the assigned asymptotic behavior of $a$ as $s	o 0^+$, given by~\eqref{ass-a}. For every $0\leq \mu<1$, we have  egin{equation} \lim_{s	o 0^+} rac{g(s)}{s^{ rac{1}{1-\mu}}}=(1-\mu)^{ rac{1}{1-\mu}} a_0^{ rac{1}{2(\mu-1)}}. \end{equation} In fact, taking into account \eqref{cauchy}, by l'H\^ opital's rule we have  egin{align*} \lim_{s	o 0^+} rac{g(s)}{s^{ rac{1}{1-\mu}}}&=(1-\mu)\lim_{s	o 0^+} rac{g'(s)}{s^{ rac{\mu}{1-\mu}}} =(1-\mu)\lim_{s	o 0^+} rac{1}{s^{ rac{\mu}{1-\mu}}\sqrt{a(g(s))}} \ & =(1-\mu)\lim_{s	o 0^+} rac{g^\mu(s)}{s^{ rac{\mu}{1-\mu}}\sqrt{a(g(s))g^{2\mu}(s)}} =  rac{(1-\mu)}{\sqrt{a_0}} \Big(\lim_{s	o 0^+}  rac{g(s)}{s^{ rac{1}{1-\mu}}}\Big)^\mu, \end{align*} which yields the claim. Moreover, by virtue of~\eqref{ass-a}, \eqref{ass-f} and \eqref{gatzero}, we have  egin{equation} \lim_{s	o 0^+} rac{h(s)}{s^{ rac{\mu-\gamma}{1-\mu}}}= \lim_{s	o 0^+} f(g(s))g(s)^{\gamma} rac{1}{\sqrt{a(g(s))g(s)^{2\mu}}} \Big[ rac{g(s)}{s^{ rac{1}{1-\mu}}}\Big]^{\mu-\gamma}= f_0 a_0^{ rac{1-\gamma}{2(\mu-1)}}(1-\mu)^{- rac{\gamma-\mu}{1-\mu}}. \end{equation} Observe also that, since $a(s)\sim a_\infty s^k$ as $s	o+\infty$ and $f(s)\sim f_\infty s^{-p}$ as $s	o+\infty$ for some $a_\infty,f_\infty>0$, $k\geq 0$ and $p>1$, if $g$ still denotes the solution to \eqref{cauchy}, we have three facts:  egin{equation} \int_1^{+\infty} rac{f(g(s))}{\sqrt{a(g(s))}}ds<+\infty, \quad \lim_{s	o 0^+} rac{f(g(s))}{\sqrt{a(g(s))}}=+\infty,\quad 	ext{$s\mapsto  rac{f(g(s))}{\sqrt{a(g(s))}}$ is nonincreasing.} \end{equation} The first property follows immediately from the limit  egin{equation*} \lim_{s	o +\infty} rac{g(s)}{s^{ rac 2{k+2}}}= ig( rac{k+2} 2  rac 1{\sqrt a_\infty}  ig)^{ rac 2{k+2}}, \end{equation*} which was proved in \cite{GlasquII}. The other properties follow by \eqref{accat0} and \eqref{ass-fg}, respectively. By virtue of \eqref{gatzero} we now prove that, for every $\gamma>1$ and $0\leq \mu<1$, there holds  egin{equation} \lim_{s	o 0^+} rac{\int_{g(s)}^{+\infty} f(\xi)d\xi}{s^{ rac{1-\gamma}{1-\mu}}}=f_0 a_0^{ rac{\gamma-1}{2(1-\mu)}}(\gamma-1)^{-1} (1-\mu)^{- rac{\gamma-1}{1-\mu}}. \end{equation} In fact, since $\int_{g(s)}^{+\infty} f(\xi)d\xi	o +\infty$ for all $\gamma>1$, it follows  egin{align*} \lim_{s	o 0^+} rac{\int_{g(s)}^{+\infty} f(\xi)d\xi}{s^{ rac{1-\gamma}{1-\mu}}}&=  rac{\mu-1}{1-\gamma}\lim_{s	o 0^+} rac{f(g(s))}{s^{ rac{\mu-\gamma}{1-\mu}}\sqrt{a(g(s))}} = rac{\mu-1}{1-\gamma}\lim_{s	o 0^+} rac{f(g(s))g^\mu(s)}{s^{ rac{\mu-\gamma}{1-\mu}}\sqrt{a(g(s))g^{2\mu}(s)}} \ & = rac{\mu-1}{(1-\gamma)\sqrt{a_0}}\lim_{s	o 0^+}f(g(s))g^\gamma(s) \lim_{s	o 0^+} rac{g^{\mu-\gamma}(s)}{s^{ rac{\mu-\gamma}{1-\mu}}} \ & = rac{\mu-1}{(1-\gamma)} rac{f_0}{\sqrt{a_0}} \lim_{s	o 0^+} rac{g^{\mu-\gamma}(s)}{s^{ rac{\mu-\gamma}{1-\mu}}} = rac{\mu-1}{(1-\gamma)} rac{f_0}{\sqrt{a_0}} \Big(\lim_{s	o 0^+} rac{g(s)}{s^{ rac{1}{1-\mu}}}\Big)^{\mu-\gamma} \ & =f_0 a_0^{ rac{\gamma-1}{2(1-\mu)}}(\gamma-1)^{-1} (1-\mu)^{- rac{\gamma-1}{1-\mu}}. \end{align*} Now, for every $\ell\geq 0$, there exists a unique solution $\phi\in C([0,+\infty))\cap C^2((0,+\infty))$ of the problem  egin{equation}  egin{cases} \displaystyle \phi'(s)=\sqrt{\ell^2+2\int_{g(\phi(s))}^{+\infty}f(\xi)d\xi}, \qquad 	ext{for $s>0$}, & \ 
oalign{\vskip4pt} \, \phi(0)=0, \quad \phi(s)>0, \qquad	ext{for $s>0$}, & \ 
oalign{\vskip6pt} \lim\limits_{s	o+\infty}\phi'(s)=\ell,\,\,\,\, \lim\limits_{s	o+\infty}\phi(s)=+\infty. & \end{cases} \end{equation} To prove this, taking into account \eqref{limzze}, it is sufficient to apply \cite[Lemma 1.3]{zhangcheng}. Notice that, in particular, the solutions to problem \eqref{asympt-prob} locally (namely for every fixed $a>0$) solve the second order problem  egin{equation}  egin{cases} \displaystyle -\phi''(s)= rac{f(g(\phi(s))}{\sqrt{a(g(\phi(s)))}}, \qquad & 	ext{for $0<s\leq a$}, \ 
oalign{\vskip4pt} \, \phi(0)=0, \quad \phi(s)>0, & 	ext{for $0<s\leq a$}. \end{cases} \end{equation} We can now prove that, for every $\gamma>1$, $0\leq\mu<1$ and $\ell\geq 0$, there holds  egin{equation} \lim_{s	o 0^+} rac{\phi(s)}{s^{ rac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}= \Big( rac{1+\gamma-2\mu}{2-2\mu}\Big)^{ rac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} f_0^{ rac{1-\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} a_0^{ rac{\gamma-1}{2(1+\gamma-2\mu)}}(\gamma-1)^{ rac{\mu-1}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} (1-\mu)^{ rac{1-\gamma}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}, \end{equation} where $\phi$ denotes the unique solution to \eqref{asympt-prob}. In fact, by l'H\^ opital's rule and \eqref{limfracintt}, we obtain  egin{align*} \lim_{s	o 0^+} rac{\phi(s)}{s^{ rac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}} &= \lim_{s	o 0^+}\Big[ rac{\phi(s)^{ rac{1+\gamma-2\mu}{2-2\mu}}}{s}\Big]^{ rac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} =\lim_{s	o 0^+}\Bigg[ rac{\phi(s)^{ rac{1+\gamma-2\mu}{2-2\mu}}}{ \displaystyle\int_0^{\phi(s)} rac{d	au}{\sqrt{\ell^2+\int_{g(	au)}^{+\infty}f(\xi)d\xi}} }\Bigg]^{ rac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} \ &=\Big( rac{1+\gamma-2\mu}{2-2\mu}\Big)^{ rac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} \lim_{s	o 0^+}\Big[\phi(s)^{ rac{\gamma-1}{2-2\mu}}\sqrt{\ell^2+\int_{g(\phi(s))}^{+\infty}f(\xi)d\xi}\Big]^{ rac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} \ &=\Big( rac{1+\gamma-2\mu}{2-2\mu}\Big)^{ rac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} \lim_{s	o 0^+}\left( rac{\ell^2+\int_{g(\phi(s))}^{+\infty}f(\xi)d\xi}{ \phi(s)^{ rac{1-\gamma}{1-\mu}} }ight)^{ rac{1-\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} \ &=\Big( rac{1+\gamma-2\mu}{2-2\mu}\Big)^{ rac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} \lim_{s	o 0^+}\left( rac{\int_{g(s)}^{+\infty}f(\xi)d\xi}{s^{ rac{1-\gamma}{1-\mu}} }ight)^{ rac{1-\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} \ 
oalign{\vskip4pt} &=\Big( rac{1+\gamma-2\mu}{2-2\mu}\Big)^{ rac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} f_0^{ rac{1-\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} a_0^{ rac{\gamma-1}{2(1+\gamma-2\mu)}}(\gamma-1)^{ rac{\mu-1}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} (1-\mu)^{ rac{1-\gamma}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}. \end{align*} We are now ready to conclude the proof of Theorem~ef{main}. In light of \cite[Theorem 1.1]{craRabTar}, since $h(s)	o +\infty$ as $s	o 0^+$ by \eqref{limzze} and $h$ is non-increasing for $s>0$ by \eqref{ass-fg}, there exists a unique positive solution $z\in C^2(\Omega)\cap C( ar\Omega)$ to $-\Delta v=h(v)$. Then $g(z)\in C^2(\Omega)\cap C( ar\Omega)$ is a positive solution to \eqref{prob}. Assume that $u_1,u_2\in C^2(\Omega)\cap C( ar\Omega)$, $u_1,u_2>0$ solve \eqref{prob}. Then $g^{-1}(u_1),g^{-1}(u_2)>0$ solve $-\Delta v=h(v)$. By uniqueness, we deduce $g^{-1}(u_1)=g^{-1}(u_2)$, in turn yielding $u_1=u_2$. By virtue of \cite[Theorem 2.2 and Theorem 2.5]{craRabTar} for any solution $v$ of $-\Delta v=h(v)$ there exist four constants $\Lambda_1,\Lambda_2,\Lambda_3,\Lambda_4>0$ such that for ${m d}(x,\partial\Omega)$ small enough, $\Lambda_1 \phi({m d}(x,\partial\Omega))\leq v(x)\leq \Lambda_2 \phi({m d}(x,\partial\Omega))$ and $|Dv(x)|\leq \Lambda_3 ig[{m d}(x,\partial\Omega)h(\Lambda_4\phi({m d}(x,\partial\Omega)))+\phi({m d}(x,\partial\Omega))/{m d}(x,\partial\Omega) ig]$, being $\phi$ a solution to \eqref{asympt-prob-ii}. On account of formula~\eqref{zerobeh}, we can find two constants $\Theta_1,\Theta_2>0$ such that, for ${m d}(x,\partial\Omega)$ small enough  egin{equation} \Theta_1 {m d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{ rac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}\leq \phi({m d}(x,\partial\Omega))\leq \Theta_2 {m d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{ rac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}, \end{equation} which yield in turn $$ \Lambda_1\Theta_1 {m d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{ rac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}\leq v(x)\leq \Lambda_2\Theta_2 {m d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{ rac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}. $$ Finally, since $g$ is increasing and $u=g(v)$, we have $$ g ig(\Lambda_1\Theta_1 {m d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{ rac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}} ig)\leq u(x)\leq g ig(\Lambda_2\Theta_2 {m d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{ rac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}} ig). $$ Finally, using \eqref{gatzero}, we obtain the desired controls on $u$. Now, from \eqref{phicontrol}, as ${m d}(x,\partial\Omega)$ is small, $$ \phi({m d}(x,\partial\Omega))/{m d}(x,\partial\Omega)\leq \Theta_2 {m d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{-{ rac{\gamma-1}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}. $$ On account of \eqref{accat0} and \eqref{zerobeh}, there exists a constant $\Theta_3>0$ such that  egin{align*} & {m d}(x,\partial\Omega)h(\Lambda_4\phi({m d}(x,\partial\Omega))) =\ & =\Lambda_4^{(\mu-\gamma)/(1-\mu)}{m d}(x,\partial\Omega) \Big[ rac{h(\Lambda_4\phi({m d}(x,\partial\Omega)))}{\Lambda_4^{(\mu-\gamma)/(1-\mu)} \phi^{(\mu-\gamma)/(1-\mu)}({m d}(x,\partial\Omega))}\Big]\phi^{(\mu-\gamma)/(1-\mu)}({m d}(x,\partial\Omega)) \ & \leq \Theta_3{m d}(x,\partial\Omega){m d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{ rac{2\mu-2\gamma}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}= \Theta_3 {m d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{-{ rac{\gamma-1}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}, \end{align*} for ${m d}(x,\partial\Omega)$ small enough, yielding $|Dv(x)|\leq \Lambda_3 (\Theta_2+\Theta_3){m d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{-{ rac{\gamma-1}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}$. Then, we have  egin{align*} |Du(x)| &=g'(v(x))|Dv(x)|= rac{|Dv(x)|}{\sqrt{a(g(v(x)))}}= rac{|Dv(x)|}{\sqrt{a(g(v(x)))g^{2\mu}(v(x))}}g^{\mu}(v(x)) &\ & = rac{1}{\sqrt{a(g(v(x)))g^{2\mu}(v(x))}} rac{g^{\mu}(v(x))}{v(x)^{\mu/(1-\mu)}}v(x)^{\mu/(1-\mu)}|Dv(x)| \leq\omega_1 v(x)^{\mu/(1-\mu)}|Dv(x)| \ 
oalign{\vskip4pt} &\leq \omega_2{m d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{ rac{2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}{m d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{-{ rac{\gamma-1}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}} =\omega_2{m d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{ rac{1-\gamma+2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}. \end{align*} for some $\omega_1,\omega_2>0$. In particular, if $1<\gamma\leq 1+2\mu$, it follows that $u$ is Lipschitz continuous up the boundary. If instead $\gamma>1+2\mu$, by the above estimates for $u$ and $|Du|$, we find $\Theta_4>0$ such that  egin{align*} |D u^{ rac{1+\gamma-2\mu}{2}}(x)|& = rac{1+\gamma-2\mu}{2}u^ rac{\gamma-1-2\mu}{2}(x)|Du(x)| \ & \leq \Theta_4 {m d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{ rac{\gamma-1-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}{m d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{ rac{1-\gamma+2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}} =\Theta_4, \end{align*} whenever ${m d}(x,\partial\Omega)$ is small enough. In turn, since $u^{ rac{1+\gamma-2\mu}{2}}$ is Lipschitz continuous, $0<2/(1+\gamma-2\mu)<1$ and $u=(u^{(1+\gamma-2\mu)/2})^{2/(1+\gamma-2\mu)}$ it follows that $u$ is H"older continuous up to the boundary $\partial\Omega$ with exponent $2/(1+\gamma-2\mu)$, as desired. Finally, concerning the Sobolev regularity of the solution $u$, observe that in light of \cite[Theorem 1.3-J2]{zhangcheng}, a necessary and sufficient condition for $v$ to belong to $H^1_0(\Omega)$ is that $$ \lim_{s	o 0^+}\int_s^1 \phi(\xi)h(\phi(\xi))d\xi<+\infty, $$ and this, since by \eqref{accat0} and \eqref{zerobeh} $ \phi(	au)h(\phi(	au))\sim 	au^{ rac{2-2\gamma}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}$ as $	au	o 0^+$, is satisfied if and only if $\gamma<3-2\mu$. In turn, $u=g(v)\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ if $\gamma<3-2\mu$ since $g$ is Lipschitz continuous on $(0,+\infty)$ being $a$ bounded away from zero. This concludes the proof of the theorem. \qed
nodes.statement_short: Change of variables $u=g(v)$ reduces (1.1) to the semilinear $-\Delta v=h(v)$, whose existence, uniqueness and boundary estimates are known; the asymptotics of $g$ and of the ODE profile $\phi$ near $0$ transfer them to $u$.

nodes.name: Cauchy problem for the change of variable g (2.1)
nodes.statement: \begin{cases} g'(s)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{a(g(s))}},\quad \text{for $s>0$}, &\\ g(0)=0, & \\ \noalign{\vskip3pt} g(s)>0, \quad\text{for $s>0$}. & \end{cases}
nodes.label: cauchy

nodes.name: Behavior of h at zero (2.3)
nodes.statement: \lim_{s\to 0^+}\frac{h(s)}{s^{\frac{\mu-\gamma}{1-\mu}}}= \lim_{s\to 0^+} f(g(s))g(s)^{\gamma}\frac{1}{\sqrt{a(g(s))g(s)^{2\mu}}} \Big[\frac{g(s)}{s^{\frac{1}{1-\mu}}}\Big]^{\mu-\gamma}= f_0 a_0^{\frac{1-\gamma}{2(\mu-1)}}(1-\mu)^{-\frac{\gamma-\mu}{1-\mu}}.
nodes.label: accat0

nodes.name: Integrability, blow-up and monotonicity of h (2.4)
nodes.statement: \int_1^{+\infty}\frac{f(g(s))}{\sqrt{a(g(s))}}ds<+\infty, \quad \lim_{s\to 0^+}\frac{f(g(s))}{\sqrt{a(g(s))}}=+\infty,\quad \text{$s\mapsto \frac{f(g(s))}{\sqrt{a(g(s))}}$ is nonincreasing.}
nodes.label: limzze

nodes.name: Behavior of the tail integral of f (2.5)
nodes.statement: \lim_{s\to 0^+}\frac{\int_{g(s)}^{+\infty} f(\xi)d\xi}{s^{\frac{1-\gamma}{1-\mu}}}=f_0 a_0^{\frac{\gamma-1}{2(1-\mu)}}(\gamma-1)^{-1} (1-\mu)^{-\frac{\gamma-1}{1-\mu}}.
nodes.label: limfracintt

nodes.name: First-order problem for phi (2.6)
nodes.statement: \begin{cases} \displaystyle \phi'(s)=\sqrt{\ell^2+2\int_{g(\phi(s))}^{+\infty}f(\xi)d\xi}, \qquad \text{for $s>0$}, & \\ \noalign{\vskip4pt} \, \phi(0)=0, \quad \phi(s)>0, \qquad\text{for $s>0$}, & \\ \noalign{\vskip6pt} \lim\limits_{s\to+\infty}\phi'(s)=\ell,\,\,\,\, \lim\limits_{s\to+\infty}\phi(s)=+\infty. & \end{cases}
nodes.label: asympt-prob

nodes.name: Second-order problem for phi (2.7)
nodes.statement: \begin{cases} \displaystyle -\phi''(s)=\frac{f(g(\phi(s))}{\sqrt{a(g(\phi(s)))}}, \qquad & \text{for $0<s\leq a$}, \\ \noalign{\vskip4pt} \, \phi(0)=0, \quad \phi(s)>0, & \text{for $0<s\leq a$}. \end{cases}
nodes.label: asympt-prob-ii

nodes.name: Behavior of phi at zero (2.8)
nodes.statement: \lim_{s\to 0^+}\frac{\phi(s)}{s^{\frac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}= \Big(\frac{1+\gamma-2\mu}{2-2\mu}\Big)^{\frac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} f_0^{\frac{1-\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} a_0^{\frac{\gamma-1}{2(1+\gamma-2\mu)}}(\gamma-1)^{\frac{\mu-1}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} (1-\mu)^{\frac{1-\gamma}{1+\gamma-2\mu}},
nodes.label: zerobeh

nodes.name: Two-sided control of phi(d) (2.9)
nodes.statement: \Theta_1 {\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{\frac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}\leq \phi({\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega))\leq \Theta_2 {\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{\frac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}},
nodes.label: phicontrol

nodes.name: Goal and standing assumptions
nodes.statement: In this section, we prove Theorem~\ref{main}. We shall assume that conditions \eqref{ass-a}-\eqref{ass-fg} hold.
nodes.statement_short: State the goal and assume (1.2).

nodes.name: Introduce the change of variable g
nodes.statement: In order to get information about existence, uniqueness and the boundary behavior of the solutions to \eqref{prob}, we convert the quasi-linear problem \eqref{prob} into a corresponding semi-linear problem through a change of variable procedure involving the Cauchy problem for $g\in C^2((0,+\infty))\cap C([0,+\infty))$, \begin{equation} \begin{cases} g'(s)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{a(g(s))}},\quad \text{for $s>0$}, &\\ g(0)=0, & \\ \noalign{\vskip3pt} g(s)>0, \quad\text{for $s>0$}. & \end{cases} \end{equation} Due to the requirement $g>0$, the solutions of~\eqref{cauchy} are unique and solve $\int_0^{g(s)}\sqrt{a(\xi)}d\xi=s$, for $s>0$. The solution is global for $s>0$ since $a$ is bounded away from zero. This procedure was also followed in \cite{GlasquII} in the framework of explosive solutions, although there $g$ is $C^2$ around the origin and defined on ${\mathbb R}$.
nodes.statement_short: Define $g$ through the Cauchy problem (2.1); it exists globally and is unique.

nodes.name: Reduction to a semilinear problem
nodes.statement: Now, since $g\in C^2((0,+\infty))\cap C([0,+\infty))$ and it is strictly increasing, it is readily seen by a direct computation that $u\in C^2(\Omega)\cap C(\bar\Omega)$ is a positive solution to \eqref{prob} if and only if $v=g^{-1}(u)\in C^2(\Omega)\cap C(\bar\Omega)$ is a positive solution to $-\Delta v=h(v)$ in $\Omega$, where we have set $h(s):=f(g(s))/\sqrt{a(g(s))}$ for $s>0$.
nodes.statement_short: $u$ solves (1.1) iff $v=g^{-1}(u)$ solves $-\Delta v=h(v)$ with $h=f(g)/\sqrt{a(g)}$.

nodes.name: Asymptotics of g at zero
nodes.statement: Let us now obtain the asymptotic behavior of the solution $g$ to problem~\eqref{cauchy} as $s\to 0^+$ depending of the assigned asymptotic behavior of $a$ as $s\to 0^+$, given by~\eqref{ass-a}. For every $0\leq \mu<1$, we have \begin{equation} \lim_{s\to 0^+}\frac{g(s)}{s^{\frac{1}{1-\mu}}}=(1-\mu)^{\frac{1}{1-\mu}} a_0^{\frac{1}{2(\mu-1)}}. \end{equation} In fact, taking into account \eqref{cauchy}, by l'H\^ opital's rule we have \begin{align*} \lim_{s\to 0^+}\frac{g(s)}{s^{\frac{1}{1-\mu}}}&=(1-\mu)\lim_{s\to 0^+}\frac{g'(s)}{s^{\frac{\mu}{1-\mu}}} =(1-\mu)\lim_{s\to 0^+}\frac{1}{s^{\frac{\mu}{1-\mu}}\sqrt{a(g(s))}} \\ & =(1-\mu)\lim_{s\to 0^+}\frac{g^\mu(s)}{s^{\frac{\mu}{1-\mu}}\sqrt{a(g(s))g^{2\mu}(s)}} = \frac{(1-\mu)}{\sqrt{a_0}} \Big(\lim_{s\to 0^+} \frac{g(s)}{s^{\frac{1}{1-\mu}}}\Big)^\mu, \end{align*} which yields the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Derive (2.2) by l'H\^opital's rule from (2.1) and (1.2).

nodes.name: Asymptotics of h at zero
nodes.statement: Moreover, by virtue of~\eqref{ass-a}, \eqref{ass-f} and \eqref{gatzero}, we have \begin{equation} \lim_{s\to 0^+}\frac{h(s)}{s^{\frac{\mu-\gamma}{1-\mu}}}= \lim_{s\to 0^+} f(g(s))g(s)^{\gamma}\frac{1}{\sqrt{a(g(s))g(s)^{2\mu}}} \Big[\frac{g(s)}{s^{\frac{1}{1-\mu}}}\Big]^{\mu-\gamma}= f_0 a_0^{\frac{1-\gamma}{2(\mu-1)}}(1-\mu)^{-\frac{\gamma-\mu}{1-\mu}}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Derive the blow-up rate (2.3) of $h$ at zero.

nodes.name: Three properties of h
nodes.statement: Observe also that, since $a(s)\sim a_\infty s^k$ as $s\to+\infty$ and $f(s)\sim f_\infty s^{-p}$ as $s\to+\infty$ for some $a_\infty,f_\infty>0$, $k\geq 0$ and $p>1$, if $g$ still denotes the solution to \eqref{cauchy}, we have three facts: \begin{equation} \int_1^{+\infty}\frac{f(g(s))}{\sqrt{a(g(s))}}ds<+\infty, \quad \lim_{s\to 0^+}\frac{f(g(s))}{\sqrt{a(g(s))}}=+\infty,\quad \text{$s\mapsto \frac{f(g(s))}{\sqrt{a(g(s))}}$ is nonincreasing.} \end{equation} The first property follows immediately from the limit \begin{equation*} \lim_{s\to +\infty}\frac{g(s)}{s^{\frac 2{k+2}}}=\big(\frac{k+2} 2 \frac 1{\sqrt a_\infty} \big)^{\frac 2{k+2}}, \end{equation*} which was proved in \cite{GlasquII}. The other properties follow by \eqref{accat0} and \eqref{ass-fg}, respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Show $h$ is integrable at infinity, blows up at $0$ and is nonincreasing (2.4).

nodes.name: Asymptotics of the tail integral of f
nodes.statement: By virtue of \eqref{gatzero} we now prove that, for every $\gamma>1$ and $0\leq \mu<1$, there holds \begin{equation} \lim_{s\to 0^+}\frac{\int_{g(s)}^{+\infty} f(\xi)d\xi}{s^{\frac{1-\gamma}{1-\mu}}}=f_0 a_0^{\frac{\gamma-1}{2(1-\mu)}}(\gamma-1)^{-1} (1-\mu)^{-\frac{\gamma-1}{1-\mu}}. \end{equation} In fact, since $\int_{g(s)}^{+\infty} f(\xi)d\xi\to +\infty$ for all $\gamma>1$, it follows \begin{align*} \lim_{s\to 0^+}\frac{\int_{g(s)}^{+\infty} f(\xi)d\xi}{s^{\frac{1-\gamma}{1-\mu}}}&= \frac{\mu-1}{1-\gamma}\lim_{s\to 0^+}\frac{f(g(s))}{s^{\frac{\mu-\gamma}{1-\mu}}\sqrt{a(g(s))}} =\frac{\mu-1}{1-\gamma}\lim_{s\to 0^+}\frac{f(g(s))g^\mu(s)}{s^{\frac{\mu-\gamma}{1-\mu}}\sqrt{a(g(s))g^{2\mu}(s)}} \\ & =\frac{\mu-1}{(1-\gamma)\sqrt{a_0}}\lim_{s\to 0^+}f(g(s))g^\gamma(s) \lim_{s\to 0^+}\frac{g^{\mu-\gamma}(s)}{s^{\frac{\mu-\gamma}{1-\mu}}} \\ & =\frac{\mu-1}{(1-\gamma)}\frac{f_0}{\sqrt{a_0}} \lim_{s\to 0^+}\frac{g^{\mu-\gamma}(s)}{s^{\frac{\mu-\gamma}{1-\mu}}} =\frac{\mu-1}{(1-\gamma)}\frac{f_0}{\sqrt{a_0}} \Big(\lim_{s\to 0^+}\frac{g(s)}{s^{\frac{1}{1-\mu}}}\Big)^{\mu-\gamma} \\ & =f_0 a_0^{\frac{\gamma-1}{2(1-\mu)}}(\gamma-1)^{-1} (1-\mu)^{-\frac{\gamma-1}{1-\mu}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Prove (2.5) by l'H\^opital's rule and (2.2).

nodes.name: Existence of the profile phi
nodes.statement: Now, for every $\ell\geq 0$, there exists a unique solution $\phi\in C([0,+\infty))\cap C^2((0,+\infty))$ of the problem \begin{equation} \begin{cases} \displaystyle \phi'(s)=\sqrt{\ell^2+2\int_{g(\phi(s))}^{+\infty}f(\xi)d\xi}, \qquad \text{for $s>0$}, & \\ \noalign{\vskip4pt} \, \phi(0)=0, \quad \phi(s)>0, \qquad\text{for $s>0$}, & \\ \noalign{\vskip6pt} \lim\limits_{s\to+\infty}\phi'(s)=\ell,\,\,\,\, \lim\limits_{s\to+\infty}\phi(s)=+\infty. & \end{cases} \end{equation} To prove this, taking into account \eqref{limzze}, it is sufficient to apply \cite[Lemma 1.3]{zhangcheng}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Zhang-Cheng Lemma 1.3, using (2.4), to get a unique solution $\phi$ of (2.6).

nodes.name: phi solves the second-order problem
nodes.statement: Notice that, in particular, the solutions to problem \eqref{asympt-prob} locally (namely for every fixed $a>0$) solve the second order problem \begin{equation} \begin{cases} \displaystyle -\phi''(s)=\frac{f(g(\phi(s))}{\sqrt{a(g(\phi(s)))}}, \qquad & \text{for $0<s\leq a$}, \\ \noalign{\vskip4pt} \, \phi(0)=0, \quad \phi(s)>0, & \text{for $0<s\leq a$}. \end{cases} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $\phi$ locally solves the second-order problem (2.7).

nodes.name: Asymptotics of phi at zero
nodes.statement: We can now prove that, for every $\gamma>1$, $0\leq\mu<1$ and $\ell\geq 0$, there holds \begin{equation} \lim_{s\to 0^+}\frac{\phi(s)}{s^{\frac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}= \Big(\frac{1+\gamma-2\mu}{2-2\mu}\Big)^{\frac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} f_0^{\frac{1-\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} a_0^{\frac{\gamma-1}{2(1+\gamma-2\mu)}}(\gamma-1)^{\frac{\mu-1}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} (1-\mu)^{\frac{1-\gamma}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}, \end{equation} where $\phi$ denotes the unique solution to \eqref{asympt-prob}. In fact, by l'H\^ opital's rule and \eqref{limfracintt}, we obtain \begin{align*} \lim_{s\to 0^+}\frac{\phi(s)}{s^{\frac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}} &= \lim_{s\to 0^+}\Big[\frac{\phi(s)^{\frac{1+\gamma-2\mu}{2-2\mu}}}{s}\Big]^{\frac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} =\lim_{s\to 0^+}\Bigg[\frac{\phi(s)^{\frac{1+\gamma-2\mu}{2-2\mu}}}{ \displaystyle\int_0^{\phi(s)}\frac{d\tau}{\sqrt{\ell^2+\int_{g(\tau)}^{+\infty}f(\xi)d\xi}} }\Bigg]^{\frac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} \\ &=\Big(\frac{1+\gamma-2\mu}{2-2\mu}\Big)^{\frac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} \lim_{s\to 0^+}\Big[\phi(s)^{\frac{\gamma-1}{2-2\mu}}\sqrt{\ell^2+\int_{g(\phi(s))}^{+\infty}f(\xi)d\xi}\Big]^{\frac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} \\ &=\Big(\frac{1+\gamma-2\mu}{2-2\mu}\Big)^{\frac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} \lim_{s\to 0^+}\left(\frac{\ell^2+\int_{g(\phi(s))}^{+\infty}f(\xi)d\xi}{ \phi(s)^{\frac{1-\gamma}{1-\mu}} }\right)^{\frac{1-\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} \\ &=\Big(\frac{1+\gamma-2\mu}{2-2\mu}\Big)^{\frac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} \lim_{s\to 0^+}\left(\frac{\int_{g(s)}^{+\infty}f(\xi)d\xi}{s^{\frac{1-\gamma}{1-\mu}} }\right)^{\frac{1-\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} \\ \noalign{\vskip4pt} &=\Big(\frac{1+\gamma-2\mu}{2-2\mu}\Big)^{\frac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} f_0^{\frac{1-\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} a_0^{\frac{\gamma-1}{2(1+\gamma-2\mu)}}(\gamma-1)^{\frac{\mu-1}{1+\gamma-2\mu}} (1-\mu)^{\frac{1-\gamma}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Prove (2.8) by l'H\^opital's rule and (2.5).

nodes.name: Existence
nodes.statement: We are now ready to conclude the proof of Theorem~\ref{main}. In light of \cite[Theorem 1.1]{craRabTar}, since $h(s)\to +\infty$ as $s\to 0^+$ by \eqref{limzze} and $h$ is non-increasing for $s>0$ by \eqref{ass-fg}, there exists a unique positive solution $z\in C^2(\Omega)\cap C(\bar\Omega)$ to $-\Delta v=h(v)$. Then $g(z)\in C^2(\Omega)\cap C(\bar\Omega)$ is a positive solution to \eqref{prob}.
nodes.statement_short: Crandall-Rabinowitz-Tartar Theorem 1.1 gives a solution $z$ of $-\Delta v=h(v)$, so $g(z)$ solves (1.1).

nodes.name: Uniqueness
nodes.statement: Assume that $u_1,u_2\in C^2(\Omega)\cap C(\bar\Omega)$, $u_1,u_2>0$ solve \eqref{prob}. Then $g^{-1}(u_1),g^{-1}(u_2)>0$ solve $-\Delta v=h(v)$. By uniqueness, we deduce $g^{-1}(u_1)=g^{-1}(u_2)$, in turn yielding $u_1=u_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Uniqueness for $-\Delta v=h(v)$ transfers to (1.1) through $g^{-1}$.

nodes.name: Boundary estimates for v
nodes.statement: By virtue of \cite[Theorem 2.2 and Theorem 2.5]{craRabTar} for any solution $v$ of $-\Delta v=h(v)$ there exist four constants $\Lambda_1,\Lambda_2,\Lambda_3,\Lambda_4>0$ such that for ${\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)$ small enough, $\Lambda_1 \phi({\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega))\leq v(x)\leq \Lambda_2 \phi({\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega))$ and $|Dv(x)|\leq \Lambda_3\big[{\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)h(\Lambda_4\phi({\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)))+\phi({\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega))/{\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)\big]$, being $\phi$ a solution to \eqref{asympt-prob-ii}.
nodes.statement_short: Crandall-Rabinowitz-Tartar give two-sided bounds on $v$ and a bound on $|Dv|$ in terms of $\phi(d)$.

nodes.name: Power-law bounds for v
nodes.statement: On account of formula~\eqref{zerobeh}, we can find two constants $\Theta_1,\Theta_2>0$ such that, for ${\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)$ small enough \begin{equation} \Theta_1 {\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{\frac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}\leq \phi({\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega))\leq \Theta_2 {\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{\frac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}, \end{equation} which yield in turn $$ \Lambda_1\Theta_1 {\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{\frac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}\leq v(x)\leq \Lambda_2\Theta_2 {\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{\frac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}. $$
nodes.statement_short: By (2.8), $\phi(d)\asymp d^{(2-2\mu)/(1+\gamma-2\mu)}$ (2.9), hence the same for $v$.

nodes.name: Bounds for u
nodes.statement: Finally, since $g$ is increasing and $u=g(v)$, we have $$ g\big(\Lambda_1\Theta_1 {\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{\frac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}\big)\leq u(x)\leq g\big(\Lambda_2\Theta_2 {\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{\frac{2-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}\big). $$ Finally, using \eqref{gatzero}, we obtain the desired controls on $u$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the increasing $g$ and (2.2) to get the two-sided bounds on $u$.

nodes.name: Gradient bound for v
nodes.statement: Now, from \eqref{phicontrol}, as ${\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)$ is small, $$ \phi({\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega))/{\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)\leq \Theta_2 {\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{-{\frac{\gamma-1}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}. $$ On account of \eqref{accat0} and \eqref{zerobeh}, there exists a constant $\Theta_3>0$ such that \begin{align*} & {\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)h(\Lambda_4\phi({\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega))) =\\ & =\Lambda_4^{(\mu-\gamma)/(1-\mu)}{\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega) \Big[\frac{h(\Lambda_4\phi({\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)))}{\Lambda_4^{(\mu-\gamma)/(1-\mu)} \phi^{(\mu-\gamma)/(1-\mu)}({\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega))}\Big]\phi^{(\mu-\gamma)/(1-\mu)}({\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)) \\ & \leq \Theta_3{\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega){\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{\frac{2\mu-2\gamma}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}= \Theta_3 {\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{-{\frac{\gamma-1}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}, \end{align*} for ${\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)$ small enough, yielding $|Dv(x)|\leq \Lambda_3 (\Theta_2+\Theta_3){\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{-{\frac{\gamma-1}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound both terms of the $|Dv|$ estimate by $d^{-(\gamma-1)/(1+\gamma-2\mu)}$ using (2.3), (2.8), (2.9).

nodes.name: Gradient bound for u
nodes.statement: Then, we have \begin{align*} |Du(x)| &=g'(v(x))|Dv(x)|=\frac{|Dv(x)|}{\sqrt{a(g(v(x)))}}=\frac{|Dv(x)|}{\sqrt{a(g(v(x)))g^{2\mu}(v(x))}}g^{\mu}(v(x)) &\\ & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{a(g(v(x)))g^{2\mu}(v(x))}}\frac{g^{\mu}(v(x))}{v(x)^{\mu/(1-\mu)}}v(x)^{\mu/(1-\mu)}|Dv(x)| \leq\omega_1 v(x)^{\mu/(1-\mu)}|Dv(x)| \\ \noalign{\vskip4pt} &\leq \omega_2{\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{\frac{2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}{\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{-{\frac{\gamma-1}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}} =\omega_2{\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{\frac{1-\gamma+2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}. \end{align*} for some $\omega_1,\omega_2>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Chain rule $|Du|=|Dv|/\sqrt{a(g(v))}$ gives $|Du|\lesssim d^{(1-\gamma+2\mu)/(1+\gamma-2\mu)}$.

nodes.name: Case $\gamma\le 1+2\mu$: Lipschitz
nodes.statement: In particular, if $1<\gamma\leq 1+2\mu$, it follows that $u$ is Lipschitz continuous up the boundary.
nodes.statement_short: For $1<\gamma\le1+2\mu$ the gradient is bounded, so $u$ is Lipschitz.

nodes.name: Case $\gamma>1+2\mu$: H\"older
nodes.statement: If instead $\gamma>1+2\mu$, by the above estimates for $u$ and $|Du|$, we find $\Theta_4>0$ such that \begin{align*} |D u^{\frac{1+\gamma-2\mu}{2}}(x)|& =\frac{1+\gamma-2\mu}{2}u^\frac{\gamma-1-2\mu}{2}(x)|Du(x)| \\ & \leq \Theta_4 {\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{\frac{\gamma-1-2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}}{\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)^{{\frac{1-\gamma+2\mu}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}} =\Theta_4, \end{align*} whenever ${\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)$ is small enough. In turn, since $u^{\frac{1+\gamma-2\mu}{2}}$ is Lipschitz continuous, $0<2/(1+\gamma-2\mu)<1$ and $u=(u^{(1+\gamma-2\mu)/2})^{2/(1+\gamma-2\mu)}$ it follows that $u$ is H\"older continuous up to the boundary $\partial\Omega$ with exponent $2/(1+\gamma-2\mu)$, as desired.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the gradient of $u^{(1+\gamma-2\mu)/2}$ to get H\"older continuity of $u$.

nodes.name: Sobolev criterion for v
nodes.statement: Finally, concerning the Sobolev regularity of the solution $u$, observe that in light of \cite[Theorem 1.3-J2]{zhangcheng}, a necessary and sufficient condition for $v$ to belong to $H^1_0(\Omega)$ is that $$ \lim_{s\to 0^+}\int_s^1 \phi(\xi)h(\phi(\xi))d\xi<+\infty, $$ and this, since by \eqref{accat0} and \eqref{zerobeh} $ \phi(\tau)h(\phi(\tau))\sim \tau^{\frac{2-2\gamma}{1+\gamma-2\mu}}$ as $\tau\to 0^+$, is satisfied if and only if $\gamma<3-2\mu$.
nodes.statement_short: By Zhang-Cheng Theorem 1.3, $v\in H^1_0$ iff $\gamma<3-2\mu$.

nodes.name: Sobolev regularity of u
nodes.statement: In turn, $u=g(v)\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ if $\gamma<3-2\mu$ since $g$ is Lipschitz continuous on $(0,+\infty)$ being $a$ bounded away from zero. This concludes the proof of the theorem. \qed
nodes.statement_short: $u=g(v)\in H^1_0$ since $g$ is Lipschitz; conclude.

nodes.name: Lipschitz continuity also for $\gamma<1$
nodes.statement: \rm We know from Theorem~\ref{main} that a solution $u$ exists unique and it is Lipschitz continuous up to $\partial\Omega$ provided that $1<\gamma\leq 1+2\mu$. On the other hand, if $\gamma<1$, combining \eqref{accat0} with \cite[Theorem 2.25]{craRabTar} any solution $v$ of $-\Delta v=h(v)$ is Lipschitz continuous, and so is $u$, since $u=g(v)$ and $g$ is Lipschitz continuous on $(0,+\infty)$ since $a$ is bounded away from zero.
nodes.statement_short: Lipschitz continuity of $u$ holds for $1<\gamma\le1+2\mu$ by Theorem 1.1 and also for $\gamma<1$ via Crandall-Rabinowitz-Tartar.
nodes.label: lipremark

nodes.name: Global estimates for u and |Du|
nodes.statement: \rm Using \cite[Theorem 1.3]{zhangcheng} in place of \cite[Theorem 2.2 and Theorem 2.5]{craRabTar} we could also state some global estimates for $u$ and $|Du|$ which are valid on the whole $\bar\Omega$ and not only in a small neighborhood of the boundary $\partial\Omega$. Precisely, under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{main}, there exist $\Lambda_1,\Lambda_2,\Lambda_3,\Lambda_4>0$ with \begin{align*} & g(\Lambda_1 \phi({\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)))\leq u(x)\leq g(\Lambda_2 \phi({\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega))), \,\,\,\,\,\,\text{for $x\in\bar\Omega,$}\\ & |Du(x)|\leq \Lambda_3\frac{\big[{\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)h(\Lambda_4\phi({\rm d} (x,\partial\Omega)))+\phi({\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega))/{\rm d}(x,\partial\Omega)\big]}{\sqrt{a(u(x))}}, \,\,\,\,\,\,\text{for $x\in\bar\Omega,$} \end{align*} where $\phi$ denotes the solution to problem~\eqref{asympt-prob}. These formulas are obtained though the monotonicity of $g$ and from $|Du(x)|=|Dv(x)|/\sqrt{a(u(x))}$ for all $x\in\bar\Omega$, following by the relation $u=g(v)$.
nodes.statement_short: Using Zhang-Cheng instead of Crandall-Rabinowitz-Tartar gives estimates for $u$ and $|Du|$ on all of $\bar\Omega$ in terms of $g$ and $\phi$.
nodes.label: globalrem

nodes.name: Convexity of superlevels of u
nodes.statement: \rm Let $v$ be a smooth positive solution to $-\Delta v=h(v)$ in $\Omega$, $v=0$ on $\partial\Omega$, where $h>0$ is as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{main}. Let us consider the map $\psi:[0,+\infty)\to [0,+\infty)$ defined by $$ \psi(s):=\int_0^s \frac{1}{\sqrt{2{\mathcal H}(\xi)}}d\xi,\qquad {\mathcal H}(s):=\int_s^{+\infty} h(\xi)d\xi, \,\,\quad\text{for $s>0$.} $$ It follows that $\psi'(s)=1/{\sqrt{2{\mathcal H}(s)}}>0$, $\psi''(s)={h(s)}/{(2{\mathcal H}(s))^{3/2}}>0$ and $\psi$ satisfies $\psi''(s)=(\psi'(s))^3 h(s)$ for all $s>0$. Put $w:=-\psi(v)<0$, we have $|Dv|^2=|Dw|^2/(\psi'(v))^2$ as well as $\Delta w =-\psi''(v)|Dv|^2+\psi'(v)h(v)=\psi'(v) h(v)(1-|Dw|^2)$, yielding \begin{equation*} \Delta w=f(w,Dw),\qquad f(w,Dw):=-\psi'(\psi^{-1}(-w)) h(\psi^{-1}(-w))(1-|Dw|^2), \end{equation*} with $w=0$ on $\partial\Omega$. Whenever $f>0$ and $z\mapsto 1/f(z,\cdot)$ is convex, one typically obtains some convexity of $w$ if $\Omega$ is convex (see \cite{kawohl}) and in turn some convexity of superlevels of $u$ since $u=g\circ\psi^{-1}(-w)$ and since $s\mapsto g\circ\psi^{-1}(s)$ is strictly increasing. See \cite[Sec.\ 3]{frapor} for the particular case $a\equiv 1$ and $f(s)=s^{-\gamma}$.
nodes.statement_short: The transform $w=-\psi(v)$ turns the problem into $\Delta w=f(w,Dw)$, from which convexity of $w$ and of superlevel sets of $u$ can typically be obtained on convex domains.
nodes.label: convexity
